summary.value: Ayam Kampong, or Ayam Kampung, means village chicken, and the name covers the free ranging native chickens kept by almost every rural household in Indonesia and Malaysia. The population is very mixed, the result of red junglefowl, local Southeast Asian birds and imported European stock crossing freely since the late 1800s. Looks vary widely, but three main types are recognized: black-red, red and naked neck. Birds are small and grow slowly. Hens weigh roughly 3 to 4 pounds and cocks 3.5 to 5, depending on the flock. Hens lay only about 55 to 100 small light brown eggs a year, largely because they go broody so often. Meat birds reach market weight of 2 to 3 pounds in three or four months, and the meat sells for more than commercial chicken. Families prize these birds for meals at celebrations and special occasions.
